import pandas as pd
import os
import re
from collections import defaultdict

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv("./input/en_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/en_test_2.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/en_sample_submission_2.csv")

# Create a held-out validation set (last 5% of train)
val_ratio = 0.05
val_size = int(len(train) * val_ratio)
train_small = train.iloc[:-val_size].copy()
val_data = train.iloc[-val_size:].copy()

# Build mapping from (before, class) -> most frequent after using training data
mapping_class = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int)))
before_class_freq = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))

for _, row in train_small.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    after = row["after"]
    cls = row["class"]
    mapping_class[before][cls][after] += 1
    before_class_freq[before][cls] += 1


# Define deterministic class inference based on token format
def infer_class_from_format(before):
    # DATE patterns: contains '/' or '-' in specific positions
    if re.match(r"^\d{1,2}[/\-]\d{1,2}[/\-]\d{2,4}$", before):
        return "DATE"
    if re.match(r"^\d{1,2}(st|nd|rd|th)$", before):
        return "ORDINAL"
    if re.match(r"^\d+$", before):
        return "CARDINAL"
    if re.match(r"^\d+:\d+$", before):
        return "TIME"
    if re.match(r"^\d+:\d+:\d+$", before):
        return "TIME"
    if re.match(r"^\$[0-9.,]+$", before):
        return "DECIMAL"
    if re.match(r"^[0-9]+[.,][0-9]+$", before) and "." in before:
        # Decimal with dot
        return "DECIMAL"
    if (
        re.match(r"^[0-9]+[.,][0-9]+$", before)
        and "," in before
        and before.count(",") == 1
    ):
        # Could be decimal or measure, but prefer decimal
        return "DECIMAL"
    if re.match(r"^[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+$", before):
        return "DATE"  # e.g., 1.1.2020
    if re.match(r"^[0-9]+/[0-9]+/[0-9]+$", before):
        return "DATE"
    if re.match(
        r"^(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?$",
        before,
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ):
        return "DATE"
    if re.match(
        r"^(Monday|Tuesday|Wednesday|Thursday|Friday|Saturday|Sunday|Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)[a-z]*\.?$",
        before,
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ):
        return "DATE"
    if re.match(r"^(AM|PM|am|pm)$", before):
        return "TIME"
    if re.match(r"^\d+(AM|PM|am|pm)$", before):
        return "TIME"
    if re.match(r"^\d+[.,]\d+[%]$", before):
        return "PERCENT"
    if re.match(r"^\d+[.,]\d+$", before):
        return "DECIMAL"
    if re.match(r"^[0-9]+[.,][0-9]+[.,][0-9]+$", before):
        return "CARDINAL"  # e.g., 1,000,000
    if re.match(r"^[A-Z][a-z]+\.$", before):
        return "ADDRESS"
    if re.match(r"^[A-Z]\.$", before):
        return "ADDRESS"
    if re.match(r"^(Mr|Mrs|Ms|Dr|Prof)\.$", before):
        return "ADDRESS"
    if re.match(r"^[A-Z][a-z]+$|[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+$", before):
        return "ELECTRONIC"  # email-like, but for simplicity treat as generic
    if (
        before.startswith("www.")
        or before.startswith("http://")
        or before.startswith("https://")
    ):
        return "ELECTRONIC"
    if (
        before == "12:47" or before == "1:00" or before == "2:30"
    ):  # common time patterns
        return "TIME"
    # Default fallback based on most frequent class for this token in training
    if before in before_class_freq:
        top_class = max(before_class_freq[before].items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
        return top_class
    return "CARDINAL"  # default for unknown tokens


# Predict on validation set using (before, class) lookup; use inferred class for validation (simulating test time)
def predict_val(row):
    before = row["before"]
    cls = infer_class_from_format(before)
    # If we have a specific (before, class) mapping, use it
    if before in mapping_class and cls in mapping_class[before]:
        candidates = mapping_class[before][cls]
        if candidates:
            return max(candidates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
    # Fall back to most frequent class for before, then its most frequent after
    if before in before_class_freq:
        top_class = max(before_class_freq[before].items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
        if before in mapping_class and top_class in mapping_class[before]:
            candidates = mapping_class[before][top_class]
            if candidates:
                return max(candidates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
    # Last resort: return before as-is
    return before


val_data = val_data.copy()
val_data["pred"] = val_data.apply(predict_val, axis=1)
accuracy = (val_data["pred"] == val_data["after"]).mean()
print(f"Validation accuracy: {accuracy:.6f}")

# Build final mapping on full training data
mapping_class_full = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int)))
before_class_freq_full = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))

for _, row in train.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    after = row["after"]
    cls = row["class"]
    mapping_class_full[before][cls][after] += 1
    before_class_freq_full[before][cls] += 1

# Generate 'id' column for test set
test = test.copy()
test["id"] = test["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test["token_id"].astype(str)


# Predict using full mapping; use deterministic class inference for test tokens
def predict_test(row):
    before = row["before"]
    cls = infer_class_from_format(before)
    if before in mapping_class_full and cls in mapping_class_full[before]:
        candidates = mapping_class_full[before][cls]
        if candidates:
            return max(candidates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
    # Fall back to most frequent class
    if before in before_class_freq_full:
        top_class = max(before_class_freq_full[before].items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
        if before in mapping_class_full and top_class in mapping_class_full[before]:
            candidates = mapping_class_full[before][top_class]
            if candidates:
                return max(candidates.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
    return before


test["after"] = test.apply(predict_test, axis=1)

# Prepare submission
submission = test[["id", "after"]].copy()
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print("Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
